_source: CORE2023 conference portal + CORE2020 legacy journal portal, verified 2026-06 (see notes)
_notes: All conference ranks verified live against the CORE2023 portal CSV export (https://portal.core.edu.au/conf-ranks/?search=<ACRONYM>&by=acronym&source=CORE2023&do=Export); journal ranks verified against the CORE2020 legacy journal portal (https://portal.core.edu.au/jnl-ranks/). Mapping of the profile's venue strings: "Companion Proceedings of the ACM on Web Conference 2025/2026" -> WWW (A*); "2024 IEEE 35th Int. Symp. on Software Reliability Engineering (ISSRE)" -> ISSRE (A); "Proceedings of the 15th International Conference on Simulation and Modeling Methodologies" -> SIMULTECH (CORE2023 C; confirmed the 15th edition = SIMULTECH 2025, Bilbao, full name "International Conference on Simulation and Modeling Methodologies, Technologies and Applications" — it is NOT ICSC); "Proceedings of the 2024 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing" -> EMNLP (A*); "Journal of Systems and Software, 112614, 2025" -> JSS (CORE2020 journal rank A — this is the defensible source for the CV's "CORE A" claim; CORE no longer maintains journal rankings, ERA2010 also rated JSS A); "International Conference on Database Systems for Advanced Applications" -> DASFAA, VERIFIED as CORE2023 B (not A); the three arXiv strings -> Preprint. Caveats: (1) Companion/workshop proceedings of WWW inherit the WWW A* label here — annotate as desired; (2) EMNLP/ACL/NAACL "Findings" tracks are not CORE-ranked, so the Findings pattern is Unranked and must precede the plain "association for computational linguistics" pattern; (3) UbiComp/IMWUT: CORE2023 lists UbiComp as "journal published" (papers appear in Proc. ACM IMWUT, which is absent from the CORE2020 journal list); the last numeric CORE rating is CORE2018 A*, reported here with that caveat; (4) known substring-collision hazards if the owner ever publishes there: PAKDD (B) contains "knowledge discovery and data mining" (KDD pattern), ICMLA (C) contains "international conference on machine learning", ICSEA (C) contains "international conference on software engineering", ICMR contains "acm international conference on multimedia" — add more-specific patterns above these if needed; (5) the venues array is in match-priority order: arXiv first, most-specific multiword patterns next, short acronym fallbacks (sigmod, sigkdd, icassp, aaai, ijcai, neurips, interspeech) placed so they only fire when the long-form pattern is absent. Apply patterns top-to-bottom against the lowercased Scholar venue string and take the first hit.
